Nutrition Intervention
As stated in the previous section, acute nutritional problems for 
stroke or aneurysm typically involve impairment in ability to 
chew, swallow, or self feed that results in inadequate nutritional 
intake. Enteral nutrition support could be necessary if an oral
diet cannot meet nutritional needs. Th is would depend on the 
severity of the stroke and the patient’s prognosis. Ethical deci-
sions concerning metabolic support (delineated in Box 20.2) 
should be addressed for patients with poor prognosis. For most
patients, evidence supports the early initiation of nutritional
support to prevent complications, reduce hospital stay, and 
promote rehabilitation (see Chapter 5). Ongoing changes in
the nutritional plan will certainly be necessary as rehabilitation 
progresses.
